name: Elaeagnaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Russian olive as an introduced comparison through silvery peltate/stellate scales, petal-less 4-lobed flowers, a tubular hypanthium and a drupe-like fruit.

project_scope.note: Species is accepted; native to eastern Europe–temperate Asia and introduced in Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the silver coating. Twigs and both leaf surfaces carry dense shieldlike/stellate scales that make the plant look metallic gray.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Shrub or small tree, often armed by thornlike lateral branches; leaves simple, narrow and densely silver-scaly.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers small, fragrant and lacking petals. Calyx/hypanthium forms a tubular 4-lobed structure; project Elaeagnus has 4 stamens.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A one-seeded achene/nutlet is enclosed by the persistent hypanthium, producing a drupe-like fleshy structure.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Metallic silvery scales + petal-less 4-lobed tubular flower + drupe-like one-seeded fruit = project Elaeagnaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: silvery scale macro → narrow leaf/twig → petal-less flower tube → fruit cutaway → introduced-status card
visual_lesson.intro: Russian olive is visually distinctive, but the learner should understand that the silver surface is made of scales and the 'drupe' is a fruit-like hypanthium surrounding the true one-seeded fruit.

steps.title: 1 · Zoom into the silver coating
steps.look_for: Overlapping peltate or stellate scales producing the silver appearance.

steps.title: 2 · Find the thornlike lateral branch
steps.look_for: Young silver-scaly twigs with some lateral branches ending as thorns.

steps.title: 3 · Prove there are no petals
steps.look_for: Four-lobed yellow-inside/silvery-outside floral tube formed by calyx/hypanthium, with 4 stamens but no corolla.
steps.why_it_matters: Corrects the assumption that the four showy lobes are petals.

steps.title: 4 · Open the drupe-like fruit
steps.look_for: Fleshy persistent hypanthium surrounding the actual one-seeded fruit.

steps.title: 5 · Keep the Texas status explicit
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents a memorable plant from becoming a false native anchor.

comparisons.title: Elaeagnaceae vs Rhamnaceae
comparisons.rule: Elaeagnaceae is immediately silver-scaly and petal-less in the project plant; Rhamnaceae generally lacks that metallic scale covering and is keyed by its nectar disc and antipetalous stamens.

visual_lesson.caveat: Silvery foliage is conspicuous but not unique in plants. Confirm the scale type and petal-less 4-lobed floral tube.

genera.fast_cue: silvery scaly leaves/twigs + petal-less 4-lobed fragrant flower + drupe-like fruit

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; native to Eurasia and introduced in Texas.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label calyx/hypanthium lobes, stamens and absence of petals
persistent hypanthium around true one-seeded fruit
